security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by markdown backticks, design terminology, or localhost screenshot URLs. The remaining confirmed issues are documented helper-script executions, hidden .claude toolchain paths, and inferred third-party image-generation prompt disclosure.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running python3 or node helper commands, and describe the exact scripts and output paths.
Avoid hardcoded hidden virtual-environment paths, or verify the script source and path before invoking them.
Warn users before sending brand, campaign, or unreleased content to external image-generation services.

Match to platform - e.g., Twitter header = `3:1` (use `3:2` closest), Instagram story = `9:16`
After designing HTML banners, export each to PNG using `chrome-devtools` skill:
- Exported PNG preview (use `ai-multimodal` skill to display if needed)
- Specify no-text: "no text, no letters, no words" (text overlaid in HTML step)
| Editorial | Media, luxury | Grid layouts, pull quotes |

content.value_statement: Teams need banners that fit each platform without losing brand clarity. This skill guides art direction, dimensions, image prompts, HTML composition, and export steps.
actual_capabilities: Collects banner purpose, platform, content, brand, style, and quantity requirements.
Uses platform size references for social covers, ads, website heroes, and print banners.
Suggests art direction styles such as minimalist, gradient, editorial, neon, and photo-based layouts.
Drafts image-generation prompts for background visuals, illustrations, product shots, and campaign art.
Composes banner concepts with HTML, CSS, text overlays, CTA placement, and safe-zone rules.
Documents PNG export steps using local preview pages and screenshot dimensions.
limitations: It depends on related design, image, and browser tooling that may not be installed.
It does not produce video, full websites, or final print production files.
External image generation may require user approval and service access.
Print guidance is directional and should be checked by a production vendor.

use_cases.title: Launch Campaign Banner Set
use_cases.description: Create coordinated social, ad, and hero banners with consistent messaging and platform-specific sizes.

use_cases.title: Refresh Social Profile Covers
use_cases.description: Design cover images for Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Facebook, and YouTube with clear safe-zone placement.

use_cases.title: Explore Visual Directions
use_cases.description: Generate several banner concepts in different styles before choosing a campaign direction.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Social Banner
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one platform and simple copy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a LinkedIn banner for our product launch. Use a clean SaaS style, this headline, and one clear CTA.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Platform Campaign
prompt_templates.scenario: Create consistent assets for several channels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three banner options for a campaign across Instagram post, Twitter/X header, and Google leaderboard sizes.

prompt_templates.title: Brand-Aware Art Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Use existing brand guidance and explore styles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use our brand guidelines and create minimalist, editorial, and photo-based banner directions for this event.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Export Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare final banners for review and export.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create HTML banner comps, generate background prompt options, export PNG previews, and summarize dimensions and rationale.

output_examples.input: A SaaS launch needs a Twitter/X header and LinkedIn banner.
output_examples.output: Three coordinated banner directions with platform dimensions, headline placement, CTA guidance, and export-ready preview paths.

output_examples.input: A conference needs bold event banners for social and website use.
output_examples.output: A bold typography direction, a photo-based direction, and a neon direction with safe zones and image prompt notes.

output_examples.input: An ecommerce brand wants Google Display ad banners.
output_examples.output: Display ad layouts for common sizes with product focus, short copy, contrast checks, and compression guidance.

best_practices: Provide platform, final size, headline, CTA, logo rules, and brand colors before design starts.
Keep critical text and logos inside the central safe zone for each platform.
Review external image-generation prompts before sending confidential campaign or brand details.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for one generic banner when each platform needs different dimensions.
Do not place important copy near edges, crops, or platform interface areas.
Do not include sensitive unreleased messaging in image prompts without approval.

faq.question: What banner types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports social covers, display ads, website hero banners, creative campaign assets, and basic print banner planning.

faq.question: Can it create several design directions?
faq.answer: Yes. It is structured to produce multiple art directions, compare them, and iterate from user feedback.

faq.question: Does it export finished PNG files?
faq.answer: It includes export steps using local HTML previews and screenshot tooling when those tools are available.

faq.question: Does it handle brand guidelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for brand context and can apply colors, typography, logo placement, and campaign tone.

faq.question: Will it make video or animated banners?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on static banner design, though it can suggest motion-ready layered concepts.

faq.question: Is external image generation required?
faq.answer: Not always. The workflow can use HTML and CSS only, but AI-generated visuals require external generation tools.
